_doc: MUTABLE routing table for Cortados. Edit freely: the router reloads this file when its mtime changes, no restart. Models, lanes and order WILL change; the six features and the band conditions come from the 2.0 scale (scale-2.0-reference.json). Validation on load: unknown lane/provider, a Fable/ceiling entry outside R4, or a non-Grok model on the cursor lane = file rejected, last good table kept.
updated_by: claude (Forest 2026-09-21: measure every pool, list every model we can reach)

subagent_policy.note: Every sub-agent is scored and routed by this same table (2.0: per_subtask_rescore). The count is a maximum; scarcity and the concurrency cap reduce it.

inventory._doc: Every model each subscription can reach, as listed by its own CLI on 2026-09-21 (full id lists in tables/inventory/). `pool` is the separately metered quota the model draws on (scarcity.py scores each pool). A model being listed here does NOT place it in a band: only `candidates` does. Unplaced models wait for a task-benchmark result or Forest's ruling (no invented tiers).

pools.fable: week (Fable): its own weekly limit on top of the all-models week

pools.all: week (+5-hour when shown). /status shows no separately limited model on this account today; any '<model> limit:' line that appears is picked up as its own pool

pools.cursor-models: Cursor's own models: Cursor Grok, Grok, Composer, Auto. Overflow spills into other-models
pools.other-models: third-party API models: Claude, GPT, Gemini, Kimi, GLM, Muse Spark

cursor.note: Claude Fable ids on Cursor are flagged NO ZDR by Cursor (no zero-data-retention): not placed.

pools.claude-gpt: Claude Sonnet/Opus 4.6 + GPT-OSS: separate 5-hour + week, untouched so far

policy_cursor._doc: Forest 2026-09-21: Cursor's third-party pool is a lane of its own. The Cursor lane accepts Grok/auto plus any id listed in tables/inventory/cursor.txt. Supersedes the 2.0 Grok-only rule for THIS system; Fable ids stay R4-only (G112) and Cursor's NO-ZDR Fable ids are not placed at all.

tiering._doc: Forest 2026-09-21 (evening): no band lists for choosing models. Every reachable model has an index per use case (tables/model-scores.generated.json, from public benchmarks weighted by tables/use-cases.json; 100 = best published model, 0 = the average published model). Every task gets a REQUIRED index (see `selection`). Bands survive only for what they were always about: hard rules, the orchestrator and how many sub-agents. band_references fix what the knots mean; `candidates` below is only the fallback if the generated file is unreadable.
tiering.refresh: weekly (Sunday night, before training) via bin/refresh-tiers.sh
tiering._live: Forest 2026-09-22: faces follow the router per turn. pre_gateway_dispatch scores with the CortadOS Router S1 service (never the 14B) and applies a one-turn model override; a degraded/slow decision leaves the configured brain in place. Set false (hot-reload) or CORTADOS_ROUTER_LIVE=0 to fall back to shadow.

selection._doc: required index for use case u = interpolation over the task's difficulty D through the knots, never below the reference of the band the hard rules put the task in (blast radius 3 / outward → Opus-class). A knot's value is the use-case index of that band's reference models (the lower of the two). All reachable models at or above the requirement qualify; the winner has the lowest cost = its GENERAL index (a heavier model is slower and burns a scarcer subscription; qualifying is by use-case index, paying is by overall weight) + scarcity_points × scarcity of the pool it draws on − expiring_bonus when that pool's headroom is about to be wiped. Spent pools are skipped. Ceiling models (general ability ≥ the R4 references) only by escalation (G112). Nothing qualifies → the strongest available model.
selection._cost: cost = weight + scarcity_points × max(scarcity,0) − expiring_credit_points × max(−scarcity,0) − capacity credit. weight = BURN: model $/1M ÷ learned pool size (tokens per % of the pool's window), normalised to 100 for the heaviest candidate (Forest 2026-09-29: pools differ ~10× in size, so price alone under-charged Claude). Falls back to price-only for pools without a learned size.
selection.r0: R0 is scored too: requirement 0, so the cheapest route wins; that is local unless a subscription window is about to expire unused.
selection._same_price_band: within one lane+pool, models whose general index is within this many points are the same price class: only the strongest of them is a candidate (Gemini 3.8 Flash over 3.6 Flash; Opus and Sonnet stay separate)
selection._lane_tiebreak: equal cost → this order: local first (a tie at R0 is the reflex case), then the lane whose pool is least fought over

primary_sources._doc: Forest 2026-09-23: native subscription first; Cursor and Antigravity's Claude/GPT pool are secondary for these vendors' models and only qualify when the native pool is spent (ok=False). Cursor is primary for Grok, Composer, Kimi, GLM, Muse and anything without a native lane here.

selection._ceiling: Forest 2026-09-23: Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra WIN BY SCORE (supersedes G112 escalation-only). The requirement reaches their index at D≥11 (a hard, high-novelty, high-ambiguity task) and any use case where only they clear the bar; their price ($20/1M Fable) keeps them off easy work. Thinking/strategy work: see the specialization file (tables/community-sentiment.json) once the nightly rating exists.
selection._sticky: a session keeps its model only while that model is within sticky_slack_points of the cheapest qualifying route; scarcity or price changes move it. Browser/desktop sessions are pinned (budgets.json stickiness) until their pool is spent.

ceiling_work._doc: Forest 2026-09-25: Fable and Astra are what the expensive subscriptions are FOR: strategic decisions and insight. Planning and research work of at least moderate difficulty (D ≥ 5) requires the R4 reference index for that use case, so only the ceiling models clear it (Astra 100/100 on planning/research, Fable 91/90). min_D 7 (Forest 2026-09-29): an outward turn already carries blast_radius 3, so D ≥ 5 caught ordinary replies tagged planning; real strategic asks (ambiguity/novelty) clear 7. Everything else keeps the price ladder, where open and mid models take what they can. Their pools' underuse credit then decides how much of the rest they attract.

ceiling_underuse._doc: when a ceiling model's own pool is underused (scarcity ≤ −0.3: the allowance would otherwise expire unused), it also takes any R3-level task (D ≥ 6) in every use case: paid-for capacity is used, not lost.

selection._capacity: Forest 2026-09-26: subscriptions are not normalised (Codex > Claude > Gemini > Cursor in absolute allowance). unitcost.py learns tokens-per-percent per pool from our own samples and ledger; among pools with room (scarcity ≤ 0), the route on the pool with the most tokens left gets up to capacity_credit_points off. Re-learned every 6 h and nightly.
selection._interactive_floor: Forest: the right answer over cost. A FACE turn (unit_kind interactive) never runs on a model below this general index even at R0 — 2026-09-27 09:13 the cheapest qualifying route (gpt-oss-120b, index 0) answered Forest's 'done' in Donna's 150k-token session with leaked reasoning. Crons and sub-agents keep the full ladder.

review_policy._doc: Explicit router_review only; no automatic reviewer fan-out. Compare the actual author model, not task difficulty. Ceiling flag defines frontier vs smaller; Samantha stays in that class within a use-case index gap, Rachel switches classes. Vendor means model maker, not subscription lane. OpenAI/Anthropic are preferred reciprocal partners; use another eligible vendor if unavailable. Never relax diversity/class for scarcity.
